description: The figure uses two pie charts to represent an error-category breakdown for two models (Vanilla on the left and HCL on the right), with each chart divided into four slices corresponding to the same set of categories. In the left pie chart, the slices are labeled Atomic Skill Fail (dark teal) at approximately 68.0%, Correct (medium teal) at 12.0%, Reason Error (light blue-gray) at 12.0%, and Question Misunderstood (very light gray/white) at 8.0%. In the right pie chart, the slices are labeled Correct (medium teal) at 55.0%, Reason Error (light blue-gray) at 21.0%, Question Misunderstood (very light gray/white) at 14.0%, and Atomic Skill Fail (dark teal) at 10.0%. A legend across the top maps colors to the four labels, and each slice contains an internal percentage label; no slices appear exploded or otherwise visually emphasized, and the slice ordering differs between the two pies rather than following a single consistent sequence.
caption_used: The figure presents an error analysis comparing the Vanilla model (left) and the HCL model (right) using pie charts. The left chart shows that the majority of errors are due to 'Atomic Skill Fail' (68.0%), followed by 'Correct' responses (12.0%), 'Reason Error' (12.0%), and 'Question Misunderstood' (8.0%). In contrast, the right chart indicates that the HCL model significantly improved performance, with 'Correct' responses increasing to 65.0%. 'Reason Error' accounts for 21.0%, while 'Atomic Skill Fail' and 'Question Misunderstood' are reduced to 10.0% and 4.0%, respectively. This suggests that the HCL model consistently outperforms the Vanilla model in addressing reasoning errors and misunderstanding questions.
